episode.title: Interrupt non-TTY subprocesses without bypassing normal lifecycle completion
episode.before: At parent f574946960a4d21e884453ac9963a869153b847d, unified exec rejected every non-empty write_stdin request for a non-TTY process as StdinClosed. Neither the unified process abstraction nor the local/remote exec-server interface exposed a non-consuming signal operation, and spawned-process handles only offered termination, which killed the process and aborted lifecycle helper tasks. Consequently an exact U+0003 Ctrl-C request could not reach a long-running non-TTY process while preserving its signal-handler output and actual exit status.
episode.after: At f2969f36e8b6aa2aefcd625d2a9fc8425bb2a519, unified exec recognizes exact U+0003 as an interrupt for non-TTY sessions while continuing to reject other non-TTY stdin. A typed interrupt operation flows through local and remote exec-server implementations to the spawned-process handle; Unix backends send SIGINT to the process group without consuming the terminator or aborting output/wait tasks, while unsupported backends return an explicit error. The existing post-write collection path then drains process output, observes closure, removes the completed session, and reports either the process handler's exit code or 128 plus the terminating signal.
episode.diff: The commit changes 19 files. It adds ProcessSignal::Interrupt and process/signal protocol, client, router, handler, registry, local-process, and remote-process support; adds a non-consuming signal method to spawned-process handles and SIGINT process-group delivery on Unix; maps signal-only ExitStatus values to 128+signal; special-cases exact U+0003 in non-TTY write_stdin before the existing output collection path; and adds local/remote exec-server plus end-to-end unified-exec tests for trapped interrupts, default SIGINT exit 130, output draining, session cleanup, and explicit Windows unsupported errors.

evidence_units.claim: Commit f2969f36 has parent f574946960 and states that non-TTY unified-exec processes could not be interrupted through write_stdin; the intended resolution is a real signal path that preserves process-reported output and exit metadata.

In the parent, write_stdin returned StdinClosed for every non-empty non-TTY input. The change defines exact U+0003 as INTERRUPT, invokes process.interrupt only for that exact payload, continues rejecting all other non-TTY input, and then proceeds through the existing output collection and state-refresh path.

UnifiedExecProcess gains an async interrupt operation that adapts the same semantic interrupt to either the direct spawned-process handle or the exec-server-backed process handle without invoking terminate, closing output, cancelling collection, or aborting helper tasks.
The exec-server contract adds typed ProcessSignal::Interrupt, SignalParams, an empty SignalResponse, and the process/signal method.

Signal requests are carried through the exec-server client/session, ExecProcess interface, remote implementation, RPC router and handler, process handler, and local process implementation, so local and remote execution share the same lifecycle operation.

evidence_units.claim: ProcessHandle::signal borrows the retained child controller rather than taking it, whereas request_terminate consumes the controller and terminate also aborts reader, writer, and wait tasks. This makes interrupt non-consuming and leaves normal output and exit observation alive.

Unix pipe and PTY backends translate Interrupt to SIGINT for the entire process group. Backends without supported signaling return an Unsupported error saying that process interrupt is not supported; hard-kill behavior remains separate.

evidence_units.claim: Exit-status normalization now preserves ordinary process exit codes and maps Unix signal termination to 128 plus the signal number, replacing the previous -1 fallback for signal-only statuses in pipe and PTY wait paths.
evidence_units.source: git diff f574946960a4d21e884453ac9963a869153b847d f2969f36e8b6aa2aefcd625d2a9fc8425bb2a519 -- codex-rs/utils/pty/src/process.rs codex-rs/utils/pty/src/pipe.rs codex-rs/utils/pty/src/pty.rs

evidence_units.claim: Exec-server integration tests exercise both local and remote backends with a non-TTY shell that traps SIGINT, emits signal:2, and exits 7; reads must retain the handler output, exit code 7, and closed state.

End-to-end unified-exec tests send exact U+0003 to non-TTY sessions and verify a trapped interrupt preserves handler output and exit code 42, a default SIGINT reports exit code 130, and the completed process is removed from the session map.
Windows-specific exec-server and unified-exec tests require non-TTY interrupt attempts to fail explicitly with the unsupported-backend message rather than pretending the process was interrupted.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-non-tty-interrupt-control-input
candidate_atomics.title: Recognize only the interrupt control payload on closed non-TTY stdin
candidate_atomics.description: Treat an exact interrupt control character as a lifecycle-control request while preserving the existing rejection of ordinary input when a non-TTY process has no writable stdin.

semantic_action.intent: Allow a caller to request interruption of a running non-TTY subprocess without reopening or weakening its closed-stdin contract.
semantic_action.pre_state: A running session is non-TTY, its ordinary stdin is unavailable, and a write-style control request contains a non-empty payload.
semantic_action.post_state: Exact U+0003 is routed as an interrupt operation; every other non-empty payload still fails as closed stdin.
semantic_action.validation: Start a long-running non-TTY session, submit exact U+0003 and observe interruption; separately retain the established oracle that ordinary non-TTY writes return StdinClosed.

candidate_atomics.name: propagate-nonconsuming-process-interrupt
candidate_atomics.title: Propagate an interrupt without consuming lifecycle ownership
candidate_atomics.description: Expose one typed interrupt operation across direct and remote process abstractions, deliver it to the Unix process group, retain output/wait machinery, and report unsupported platforms explicitly.

semantic_action.intent: Deliver a graceful interrupt to the subprocess and its descendants while keeping the session alive long enough to observe the process's own response.
semantic_action.module_role: subprocess lifecycle-control transport and backend adapter
semantic_action.pre_state: A process handle remains registered and owns a child controller plus active output and exit observers.
semantic_action.post_state: Supported backends receive an interrupt at process-group scope without consuming the controller or aborting observers; unsupported backends return a specific capability error; hard termination remains a distinct operation.
semantic_action.validation: Across local and remote backends, a shell SIGINT handler must run, emit output, exit with its chosen code, and close normally; on an unsupported backend the request must return the documented unsupported error.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-interrupt-completion-metadata
candidate_atomics.title: Drain interrupted-process output and preserve its real exit result
candidate_atomics.description: After sending the interrupt, continue the normal collection and completion path so handler output and actual exit metadata determine the result, including conventional 128-plus-signal status for default Unix signal termination.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent control handling from fabricating an exit code, discarding late output, or clearing the session before the subprocess reaches an observable terminal state.
semantic_action.pre_state: An interrupt has been delivered while output readers and the process wait observer remain active.
semantic_action.post_state: Available output is drained, normal closure is observed, the completed session is cleared, explicit handler exit codes are retained, and signal-only Unix termination is represented as 128 plus the signal number.
semantic_action.validation: A trapped interrupt must expose its final output and custom exit code; a default SIGINT must report 130; both results must omit a live process identifier after completion.

candidate_workflows.name: add-lifecycle-safe-non-tty-interrupt
candidate_workflows.title: Add lifecycle-safe interruption for a non-TTY subprocess
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for translating a write-style interrupt sentinel into a real subprocess signal while maintaining stdin restrictions, transport parity, output draining, exit-status fidelity, session cleanup, and explicit platform limitations.

workflow_graph.goal: Let a caller interrupt a long-running non-TTY subprocess through an existing session-control surface and receive the subprocess's genuine final output and exit metadata.
when_to_use: A long-running process is managed as a persistent session but was launched without a TTY or writable stdin.
The existing control surface represents Ctrl-C as an exact control-character payload.
Graceful interruption must run process signal handlers and preserve normal output and exit observation across local or remote execution.
anti_goals: Do not enable arbitrary stdin writes for processes whose stdin is closed.
Do not replace interrupt with hard termination or abort lifecycle observers immediately after signaling.
Do not fabricate a Ctrl-C exit code when the process can report its own handler-selected exit code.
Do not silently claim interrupt support on a backend that cannot implement it.
Do not redesign unrelated process start, read, termination, or hard-kill semantics.
not_applicable_when: The process is attached to an interactive TTY whose existing input path already provides terminal Ctrl-C semantics.
The request is ordinary process input rather than the exact interrupt sentinel.
No retained process handle or backend signaling capability exists and the caller cannot accept an explicit unsupported result.
Immediate unconditional hard-kill, rather than graceful interrupt handling and result collection, is the required behavior.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A non-TTY subprocess remains registered and running, ordinary stdin writes are closed or rejected, and the caller needs Ctrl-C-like interruption without losing lifecycle evidence.
workflow_graph.exit_state: On a supported backend the process group has received the interrupt, final output and authentic exit metadata have been collected, and a completed process is removed from the session registry; on an unsupported backend the caller receives a specific capability error without a fabricated successful interruption.

steps.condition: The request targets a non-TTY session and contains non-empty write-style input.
steps.validation: Exact U+0003 selects interrupt handling, while another non-empty payload retains the closed-stdin failure.

steps.condition: The payload was classified as an interrupt and the process remains addressable.
steps.validation: Local and remote Unix-backed executions invoke a signal handler without terminating observer tasks; unsupported backends return the explicit unsupported error.

steps.condition: Interrupt delivery succeeded and lifecycle observers remain active.
steps.validation: Handler output and custom exit code are retained, default SIGINT produces 130, closure is observed, and no live session identifier remains.

validation_ladder: Unit/contract level: confirm the process abstraction accepts the typed interrupt operation while ordinary non-TTY input remains rejected.
Backend integration level: run a non-TTY process with a SIGINT trap through both local and remote execution; require trap output, its chosen exit code, and closed state.
End-to-end lifecycle level: send exact U+0003 through the session-control tool; require drained trap output, authentic exit metadata, and removal of the completed session.
Default-signal level: interrupt a process without a handler and require conventional Unix exit code 130.
Capability boundary: on an unsupported backend, require a model-visible unsupported-interrupt error and no fabricated success.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the session cannot distinguish the exact interrupt sentinel from ordinary input.
Stop and report unsupported if the backend cannot deliver the requested signal; do not fall back silently to hard-kill.
Stop and treat the implementation as incomplete if signaling consumes the process controller or aborts output/wait observers before final state is collected.
Stop and treat validation as failed if handler output, handler-selected exit status, default signal status, or session cleanup is lost.
unresolved_or_deferred: The bundle does not include CI results or logs proving that the validation commands recorded in the commit completed successfully.
The implemented signal vocabulary contains only Interrupt; behavior and portability for additional signal types remain outside this episode.
Windows non-TTY interruption remains explicitly unsupported by this change.

unresolved_questions: Were all validation commands listed in the commit executed successfully? The GitHub bundle omits status checks and contains no test logs.
